Services

Company registration

Registering a company in Australia means applying to ASIC for an ACN. We handle the application, the share structure and the director IDs, and you get the certificate of registration, constitution and company register.

Our fee

Quoted before we start

Fixed, agreed in writing, no work begins before you accept it.

Government charges

Payable on top

ASIC charges a company registration fee, paid to the government on top of ours. We tell you the current amount before you commit.

Who does it

A registered tax agent

BRS Advisory Pty Ltd, agent 26233684, CPA Australia Practice.

What’s included

  • Company name availability check and reservation
  • ASIC registration and your certificate of incorporation
  • Constitution, share structure and member register
  • Director ID guidance for each director
  • TFN, ABN and GST registration for the new company
  • A plain explanation of what changes at tax time once you are a company

How it runs

  1. 01 Tell us the proposed name, the directors and how you want shares split.
  2. 02 We check the name is available and confirm the structure makes sense for what you are actually doing.
  3. 03 We lodge with ASIC and register the company for its TFN and ABN.
  4. 04 You get the certificate, constitution and register, plus what to do next.

Start it

Tell us what you need and we will come back with a fixed fee and what we need from you. No obligation, and no charge for telling you that you don’t need this.

Form not loading? Open it in a new tab, or call 0407 179 179 and we will take the details over the phone. Please don’t include your tax file number either way — we ask for it securely once an accountant is working on your file.

Work the numbers first

  • Sole trader

    Tax on your business profit, plus what to put aside for GST and the next PAYG instalment.

Other services

ABN application GST registration Bookkeeping Trust setup Partnership setup Self-managed super fund All services

Registered tax agent

A real practice, not a form that emails you a PDF

Every return is prepared and reviewed by a registered agent before it is lodged. Because we lodge on your behalf, you get the agent deadline rather than the 31 October one — that is roughly six extra months, and it is the single most common reason people switch.
